where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.29.0, rulings 292, 293 and 294

where: data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx, the Automation cells of 28 rows; the blocks are printed in foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md (0.28.0) and AUTOMATION_GRAMMAR.md section 5

Twenty-eight rows have a block written for them (Stand and Kip Up: [REQUIRES prone or supine]; Grapple: [REQUIRES free hand or weapon grapple][REQUIRES creature in reach]; and the rest), and three more are a judgement about how the table plays (Release, Sneak, Battle Cry).

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.28.0, rulings 283, 286, 287 and 289; module/rules/requires.mjs, module/helpers/situation.mjs
question: Four readings the Maneuvers tab makes that Mike did not rule on. 283: a row is left out only when the system KNOWS it does not apply (no token on the map, an unsure hand count and a Blinded character hide nothing). 286: a row with a Trigger and no Reaction mark in its Cost cell (Battle Cry, Sure Seat, Steady the Line) is kept on the list off-turn as a Reaction, though the engine still gates and charges it as a plain Maneuver. 287: who is near is every other token the character's own token can see, edge to edge, never one hidden from the players, a party token or a dead body; a free hand is an estimate. 289: nothing is refused (a dimmed row can be used), and an owned copy of a Basic Maneuver is listed in place of the Basic row.
recommendation: Leave all four. 286 goes away when the rows' Cost cells carry the Reaction mark, which also settles the open point of 0.23.0 for the engine.

where: System 0.27.0, rulings 276, 277 and 280 (foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md)
question: Three rulings of 0.27.0 are Claude's readings, not Mike's answers. 276: a Strike that "resolves before the Bind ends" keeps the Zone the Control held open on its own result card, and the Bind ends before that card (a damage button may never be pressed). 277: Close needs no click, any Step by the Controller that ends nearer the foe is the Close. 280: Gain Control takes no -2 for a Controlled implement, and a fighter who already Controls cannot use it. Do they stand?
recommendation: Let all three stand. 276 and 277 remove a decision and a click with no cost; for 280, say so if a Controlled fighter's Gain Control should be the harder roll, and the -2 is one line.

where: module/documents/actor/bind.mjs (one Bind for each fighter); module/documents/actor/wounds.mjs, rigidImplement (a held shield before any weapon)
question: The book says "Track no more than one Bind per implement", so a fighter with a sword and a shield could hold two. The system holds one Bind for each fighter, and when a card forms it the implement is the shield if one is held. So a neutral Bind on the shield ends when its bearer Strikes with the sword, and a foe who Controls the shield puts no -2 on the sword. Is one Bind for each fighter enough, and should the defender choose which implement Guarded?
recommendation: Keep one Bind for each fighter until play asks for two. Add the implement choice to the card's Form a Bind and Take Control only if shield-bearers find the shield-first rule costs them; Form a Bind on the sheet already lets the player name the sword.

where: Gain Control (module/documents/actor/bind.mjs) and the other Maneuvers with the Attack trait that roll a check: Disarm, Grapple, Trip, Shove
question: A Maneuver with the Attack trait that rolls a check (Gain Control's Melee, Disarm's Athletics) takes none of the attacker's attack penalties today: an Arms Wound's -2 to attacks, Fatigued, the Arms' Critical Hit effect. An adversary's Gain Control does take the Arms' Critical Hit effect, since it reads the Attack Threshold. Should the Attack trait bring those penalties onto the check?
recommendation: Yes, as one rule for every Attack-trait check, decided once: it would make an injured arm matter in a grapple and in the Bind alike. Until then none applies, which is how every such Maneuver has always rolled.

where: module/rules/kinds/bonus.mjs, the Defense branch of a check; ruling 222 (0.21.0)

Should a bonus to every check, and a bonus to a Maneuver made without its Item, also reach a Defense rolled as a check (Wind's Endure, a Recovery, a Search with Awareness)? Today neither does: nothing is applied and nothing is offered there.
recommendation: Yes, as its own ruling, with a Wind roll driven live, because it changes numbers outside Aid.

where: module/rules/kinds/substitute.mjs, the third descriptor of USE; rulings 219 and 111

When a Talent wants a Constellation as the check a USE names, does the swap carry into an Initiative rolled with that Constellation? Ruling 111 (an Initiative rolled with a Constellation carries every modifier of that Constellation's check) argues yes.
recommendation: Settle it with the first Talent that names one; the refusal stands until then.

where: World setting "Track the six-action round" (trackActions)
question: The setting has only ever switched off the spending for movement, and since 0.23.0 for a Maneuver used from the sheet (ruling 236). Strikes, Casts, Reactions, Raise a Shield, Recenter and drawing or stowing a weapon are paid whether it is on or off, although its hint said otherwise until 0.23.0. Should Off stop those as well?
recommendation: Leave it as it is. A Strike or a Cast is declared through the attack flow, which refunds on Cancel and reads the pool, so an unpaid Strike would be a second path to keep right; a table that wants no counting can ignore the pips, which nothing enforces.

where: data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx Cost cells: Battle Cry, Lost in the Dark, Reliable Anchor, Steady the Line, Sure Seat, Quick Tongue, No Quarter, Grab an Edge
question: These rows have a Trigger and no Reaction glyph in their Cost, so the system reads each as a plain Maneuver. Since 0.23.0 a plain Maneuver used from the sheet pays its cost, so the five that cost one action pay it from their row and wait for the GM off-turn (Quick Tongue pays from its card button; the two at nought pay nothing). The same is true of any row whose empty Cost cell reads as one action.
recommendation: Write the cost with its Reaction glyph in each Cost cell (Battle Cry is nought with the glyph in the book). A Reaction is paid the moment it is used and never waits for the GM.

where: foundry/starwrought/module/documents/item.mjs, the Reaction branch of a Maneuver's use

recommendation: If such a row returns: used at your own Opportunity it is the Maneuver and pays the printed cost; used at any other time it is the Reaction and pays the half. Say the word and it is a small change.

where: module/rules/effects.mjs, the EFFECT condition; module/rules/given.mjs, the used Effect (0.25.0, ruling 247)

Step two is his Fantasy Grounds idea in full: a Maneuver puts a named Effect on its target for a duration, and CHECK, DEF and ATK lines apply IF: EFFECT(<name>) on the owner or IFT: EFFECT(<name>) on the other party.
recommendation: Plan it on its own when the first row wants it (Unbroken Courage and Rallying Word's options are candidates). It needs a tag for granting an Effect, a writer for another player's character (the Give relay is the model) and a decision on whether Oathbound's MARK folds into it.

where: data/talents_magic.xlsx (the Targets column is prose); module/canvas/area-targets.mjs; PHB v4.25, Area Attacks

The book's own clauses wait for data: "Unless the Talent specifies otherwise" (no Talent can ask for one roll for all), a spell's own shape and size, and "an area Attack does not automatically gain these location-specific effects" (the system cannot tell an area Attack from another, so its Critical Hit effect is the GM's to switch off).

where: v4.25-sync-report.md, rulings 256 and 260
question: Two readings the sync made that the book does not settle. 256: two overlapping Difficult regions of the SAME kind are two effects (x3), as two of different kinds are. 260: every Critical Hit that does damage sets its Zone's effect, an area Attack's included, and the Zone's switch on the sheet is the GM's remedy.
recommendation: Leave both unless play says otherwise; 256 is the one most likely to be argued (one circumstance counted once would make two mud regions x2).

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.32.0, rulings 313 to 318, 320 and 321
question: Readings 0.32.0 made so that APPLY and REMOVE could be built. 313: a Condition already on by other means (the GM's hand, a Critical Hit, a Bind) is left alone, nothing added and nothing taken off by a window. 314: of two APPLYs of one Effect the later window stands. 315: Dropping Prone by choice is not stopped by an IMMUNE line and does not use it up; a Prone by a Trip's result is. 316: an Effect with a window is put on only in an encounter the user or the recipient is fighting in. 317: frightened 2 on a creature already Frightened 3 changes nothing. 318: outside an encounter a row with a range of costs asks which version this use is. 320: an applied named Effect shows on everyone's hover card. 321: APPLY on a target needs IF: RESULT, and a row the system runs another way (Strike, Rush's drag) applies nothing.
recommendation: Leave them unless play says otherwise. The two most likely to be argued are 313 (a Demoralize does nothing to a creature the GM already made Frightened by hand at a lower value: it raises it, but puts no window on it) and 321 (Rush's Off-Guard is still by hand).

where: data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx (Talk Them Down, Anticipate, Bolster, Feint, Tumble Through); AUTOMATION_GRAMMAR.md section 5, Putting Effects on
question: APPLY puts an Effect on a creature, but a Basic Maneuver's row cannot make that Effect DO anything for everyone: 'it takes -2 to its next Attack against you' needs a line on the creature that reads the Effect, and such a line lives on a Talent or an owned Maneuver. The same gap leaves the Wrong-Footed Condition's own effect (Off-Guard against that creature only) to the table, though Feint now records who Wrong-Footed whom.
recommendation: Plan it as the next step in two parts. First the small one: treat Wrong-Footed applied by X as Off-Guard against X in the Defense read, since the record now says who. Then an Effect that carries its own lines, written on the APPLY line's row, so Talk Them Down and Anticipate can be automated from a Basic row.
